title: The Larzac Tablet, Continued
subtitle: Parsing AVDE, ADSAXSATILIN, and the syntax of binding.
objectives: Translate the verb AVDE ("invokes" or "calls upon").
Recognize the accusative case in the list of cursed women.
Understand the syntactic structure: X invokes Y (dative) against Z (accusative).

sections.heading: The core verb: AVDE
sections.body:
The Larzac Tablet pivots on one verb: AVDE. The word appears after the list of supernatural forces:

IN ALCVINOM CANTOBEDNNABOGAITIRCON NOILBINACON NATARCON DAXTECXXTONIAVDEDASETI

Isolating AVDE:
DAXTECXXTONI — "to the lower ones" (dative, spirits of the underworld?)
AVDE — "invokes" or "calls upon" (verb, 3rd person singular or plural)
DASETI — possibly "binds" or "places" (verb, meaning uncertain)

AVDE is cognate with Latin voveo ("I vow") and related to the Gaulish formula AVVOT ("vowed"). Here it means "invokes" or "calls upon". The cursers are calling upon the supernatural forces (all in the dative) to act.

sections.heading: ADSAXSATILIN — the binders
sections.body:
Later in the tablet, the text gives a name or description for the forces invoked:

ADSAXSATILIN

Parsing:
ADSAXSATILIN — "the ones who bind" or "the binding ones" (participle or adjective, accusative plural feminine?)

The root is *sax- ("bind"), related to Latin sancio and Old Irish sáithe. The prefix AD- intensifies. The suffix -LIN marks a participle or agent noun. These are the spirits who bind the cursed women, who prevent them from acting, speaking, or prospering.

sections.heading: The cursed women
sections.body:
After invoking the powers, the tablet lists the women to be cursed. They are in the accusative case (the direct object of the binding):

PAVLLAM PRIMAM
AIONAS ADIEGIASAS
SATIRICNAM
TERTIÁM

Parsing:
PAVLLAM — accusative singular, "Paulla" (a Latin name)
PRIMAM — accusative singular, "Prima" ("first", a Latin name or epithet)
AIONAS — accusative plural, "the Aionae" (a group name or family name)
ADIEGIASAS — accusative plural, "of Adiegias" (genitive or ethnic, modifying AIONAS)
SATIRICNAM — accusative singular, "Satiricna" (a Gaulish name)
TERTIÁM — accusative singular, "Tertia" ("third", a Latin name)

These women are the targets. The binding spirits (ADSAXSATILIN) are invoked against them.

sections.heading: The syntactic structure
sections.body:
The Larzac Tablet follows a curse formula:

1. IN + place (accusative): "in/into the sacred place"
2. Spirits invoked (dative): "to X, to Y, to Z"
3. Verb (AVDE): "(she/they) invoke(s)"
4. Targets (accusative): "Paulla, Prima, the Aionae, Satiricna, Tertia"
5. Purpose or result: "that they be bound"

This is the structure of every Roman-world defixio. The Larzac Tablet is Gaulish in language, Roman in form.

items.answer: "Invokes" or "calls upon" — the core verb of the curse.
"The ones who bind" or "the binding ones" — a description of the spirits invoked.

items.prompt: What case are the cursed women in?
items.answer: Accusative — they are the direct objects of the binding.

items.prompt: Name three of the cursed women.
items.answer: Paulla Prima, Satiricna, Tertia (also AIONAS ADIEGIASAS, a group).

items.prompt: What is the root of ADSAXSATILIN?
items.answer: *sax-, meaning "bind", related to Latin sancio and Old Irish sáithe.

items.prompt: What case are the spirits invoked in?
items.answer: Dative — they are the recipients of the invocation.

items.prompt: What is the syntactic structure of the curse?
items.answer: IN + place, spirits (dative), AVDE, targets (accusative), purpose/result.

sections.instructions: These are the key forms from the curse syntax. Memorize them.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark complete when you can translate AVDE, parse ADSAXSATILIN, and identify the accusative case in the list of cursed women.
